newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade, dealers said on Monday.
They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. March new home sales data, which are forecast to be around 794,000 units compared with 811,000 units reported in February.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for tonight's new home sales figures for fresh clues to market direction, but unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact," a local dealer said.
"Some traders are also waiting for possible direction from this Friday's (U.S. April) employment report," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Monday/Tuesday and Tuesday/Wednesday eased 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, respectively.
Week-fixed was unchanged from last Friday's 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4, nine-months unchanged at 6-1/4 6-1/8 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-7/16 6-5/16 percent. - P. Theseira (65-870-3085)
